title: Backdated Tier Start from the Qualifying Listing Date — Host Accounts
content:
# Host Fees Accounting — Tier Start of a Re-Rating by Qualifying Date (Host Accounts)

## Rule

The tier start of a re-rating of a Host Accounts holder's host service fees is worked out by one of three methods, the account's **qualifying date** being the first-listed date of its most recently first-listed listing that is listed (from the host's Listings records), and the **move** being the account's move into its tier (its latest tier-change date):

1. when the account qualified **fewer than 30** calendar days before the move, the tier start is the qualifying date;
2. when it qualified **at least 30 but fewer than 90** calendar days before the move, the tier start is 30 calendar days before the date of the move;
3. otherwise the tier start is not brought forward.

A stay assessed on or after the tier start is re-rated.

## Dated cases (hypothetical move on 15 June)

| Qualifying date | Days before the move | Tier start | A stay assessed on 20 May |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 June | 14 | 1 June | Not on or after the tier start |
| 20 April | 56 | 16 May (30 days before 15 June) | On or after the tier start |
| 16 May | 30 | 16 May (30 days before 15 June) | On or after the tier start |
| 1 February | 134 | Not brought forward | — |

## Points of judgement

- Only listings that are listed count for the qualifying date; a snoozed or unlisted listing's first-listed date is not read.
- The qualifying date is the latest first-listed date among those listings, not the earliest.
